findings.title: Routine cleanup batches are logged at Error level, including full ID lists
findings.body: The new cleanup code logs every normal batch operation with r.log.Error (lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576, 579), e.g. r.log.Error("Annotations to clean by time", "count", len(ids), "ids", ids, "cond", cond, "err", err) where err is nil on success. Since this job runs periodically and logs every batch including the complete list of annotation IDs (which can be tens of thousands of entries with large AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize values), production error logs will be flooded with huge, non-error messages. This makes real errors hard to spot and can cause significant log ingestion cost. These should be Debug-level logs, and the full ID list should likely be omitted or truncated.

findings.title: Cleanup ticker changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute, affecting all cleanup jobs
findings.body: The PR changes the main cleanup ticker from time.Minute*10 to time.Minute*1. This is not mentioned in the PR description, which is scoped to the annotation deadlock fix, and it does not only affect annotation cleanup: every job in the list (temp file cleanup, expired snapshots, dashboard versions, expired images, user invites, short URLs, query history) now runs 10x more frequently. Each run also acquires the server lock and performs database scans/deletes, so this is a meaningful load increase across the whole instance. If the intent was only to run annotation cleanup more often, this should be done separately or at least justified and called out.

findings.title: MaxCount cleanup uses OFFSET on a moving table without a transaction, which can over-delete under concurrent inserts
findings.body: The max-count cleanup now does SELECT id ... ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT batchSize OFFSET maxCount followed by a separate DELETE, with no shared transaction between the two (by design). Unlike the max-age cleanup, which is time-based and self-correcting, the OFFSET-based query is sensitive to concurrent inserts: rows inserted between the SELECT and DELETE shift the window, and because the loop re-runs immediately, freshly inserted annotations can be selected and deleted in a later batch even when the total count is at or below maxCount after earlier deletions. The comment acknowledges under-deletion but not over-deletion of recent rows. The old single-statement form at least evaluated the set atomically per batch. Consider bounding the delete to IDs known to be beyond the kept set (e.g. capture the ID at position maxCount once per run and delete only ids below it), or documenting/accepting this explicitly.
